chunks: From him, from Abi Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abi Salamah Salim ibn Mukram, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
A man said to him, while I was present, "Make the private parts lawful for me." So Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام was alarmed.

Then a man said to him, "He is not asking you to waylay the road. Rather, he is only asking you about a servant-girl whom he buys, or a woman whom he marries, or an inheritance that comes to him, or trade, or something that was given to him."

He said, "This is halal for our Shi'ah—the present among them and the absent, the dead among them and the living; whoever is born from among them until the Day of qiyamah, it is halal for them. By Allah, it is not halal except for the one for whom we have made it halal. And by Allah, we have not given anyone a guarantee of protection, nor is there between us and anyone any favoritism, nor does anyone have a covenant with us."

key_terms.الْفُرُوجَ: private parts; here, a legal expression referring to marital or slave-concubine permissibility
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: lawful and permitted by authorized dispensation
key_terms.ذِمَّةً: a guarantee, liability, or covenant of protection
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.مِيرَاثًا: inheritance that comes into one's possession

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in al-Istibsar say about what the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام made halal from khums for their Shi'ah during the ghaybah?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal dispensation granted by the Imams عليهم السلام to their Shi'ah concerning matters connected to khums in circumstances such as purchase, marriage, inheritance, trade, and gifts. It emphasizes that this permissibility is specifically by their authorization and is not a general license for all people.
